name: St. Agnes of Rome
patronage: Young Girls, Chastity, Betrothed Couples, Girl Guides
summary: Twelve-year-old Roman maiden who consecrated her virginity to Christ and joyfully embraced martyrdom during Diocletian's persecution.

name: St. Aidan of Lindisfarne
profession: Bishop of Lindisfarne & Apostle of Northumbria
summary: Irish monk from Iona who founded the monastery on Holy Island (Lindisfarne) at the request of King Oswald, evangelizing the kingdom of Northumbria on foot.

name: St. Albert the Great
profession: Dominican Friar, Bishop & Universal Doctor (Doctor Universalis)
patronage: Scientists, Philosophers, Natural Sciences, Medical Technicians
summary: Renowned Dominican scholar and mentor of St. Thomas Aquinas. He mastered theology, philosophy, physics, botany, and zoology, demonstrating harmony between faith and reason.

name: St. Aloysius Gonzaga
patronage: Catholic Youth, Students, AIDS Patients and Caregivers, Purity
summary: Italian aristocrat who renounced his noble inheritance to enter the Society of Jesus, dying at age twenty-three from the plague contracted while caring for the sick.

name: St. Alphonsus Liguori
patronage: Confessors, Moral Theologians, Lawyers, Scrupulous Persons
summary: Founder of the Congregation of the Most Holy Redeemer (Redemptorists). Master of moral theology and author of beloved devotional classics like The Glories of Mary.

name: St. Ambrose of Milan
profession: Bishop of Milan & Latin Church Father
summary: Eloquent preacher and administrator who defended orthodoxy against Arianism and baptized St. Augustine of Hippo. One of the four original Latin Doctors.

name: St. Anastasia of Sirmium
summary: Noble Roman matron who ministered to persecuted Christians in prisons and was martyred at Sirmium; traditionally commemorated at Christmas Day dawn Mass and in the Roman Canon.

name: St. André Bessette (Brother André of Montreal)
profession: Congregation of Holy Cross Lay Brother & Doorkeeper
patronage: Caregivers, Family Members, Montreal, St. Joseph's Oratory
summary: Humble Holy Cross doorkeeper at Notre Dame College in Montreal whose deep devotion to St. Joseph led to thousands of miraculous cures and the founding of Saint Joseph's Oratory.

name: St. Andrew the Apostle
summary: Brother of Simon Peter who first recognized Jesus as the Messiah and brought Peter to Him. Martyred on an X-shaped cross.

name: St. Anselm of Canterbury
profession: Benedictine Abbot, Archbishop of Canterbury & Philosopher (Doctor Magnificus)
summary: Originator of the ontological argument for the existence of God and father of Scholasticism, famous for the principle of 'fides quaerens intellectum' (faith seeking understanding).

name: St. Anthony of Padua
profession: Franciscan Priest, Preacher & Evangelical Doctor (Doctor Evangelicus)
patronage: Lost Things, the Poor, Travelers, Sailors, Lisbon
summary: Famed Franciscan orator celebrated for profound biblical knowledge, powerful preaching, and numerous miracles.

name: St. Anthony the Great
profession: Desert Father & Patriarch of Christian Monasticism
patronage: Monks, Skin Diseases, Basket Makers, Butchers, Domestic Animals
summary: Father of all monks who renounced his worldly wealth to live in the Egyptian desert, enduring spiritual warfare and inspiring generations of hermits.

name: St. Apollonia
summary: Elderly deaconess of Alexandria whose teeth were violently extracted during an anti-Christian uprising before she willingly threw herself into the flames rather than renounce Christ.

name: St. Athanasius of Alexandria
profession: Patriarch of Alexandria & Theologian (Doctor of the Incarnation)
summary: Staunch defender of the divinity of Christ against the Arian heresy at the Council of Nicaea (325). Endured five exiles for Catholic orthodoxy.

name: St. Augustine of Hippo
profession: Bishop of Hippo, Theologian & Doctor of Grace (Doctor Gratiae)
patronage: Theologians, Printers, Brewers, Searchers of Truth
summary: Converted through the prayers of St. Monica and guidance of St. Ambrose. Author of Confessions and The City of God, towering figure in Christian thought.

name: St. Barbara
patronage: Miners, Artillerymen, Firefighters, Architects, Sudden Death
summary: Early martyr imprisoned in a tower by her pagan father for embracing Christianity; venerated as one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers invoked against sudden death and lightning.

name: St. Barnabas
profession: Apostle & Missionary Companion of St. Paul
summary: Early Christian disciple and apostle who introduced St. Paul to the Jerusalem community and undertook the first missionary journey to Cyprus and Asia Minor.

name: St. Bartholomew the Apostle
summary: Identified with Nathanael of Cana, praised by Jesus as 'an Israelite in whom there is no guile'. Preached in Armenia and India, where he was flayed and martyred.

name: St. Basil the Great
profession: Bishop of Caesarea, Monastic Founder & Cappadocian Father
summary: One of the three Cappadocian Fathers. Formulated the definitive Eastern monastic rule and vigorously defended the divinity of the Holy Spirit.

name: St. Bede the Venerable
profession: Benedictine Monk, Historian & Scriptural Scholar (Doctor Anglorum)
summary: Monk of Wearmouth-Jarrow and author of the Ecclesiastical History of the English People. The only English native Doctor of the Church.

name: St. Benedict of Nursia
summary: Founded Monte Cassino and wrote the famous Rule of Saint Benedict based on 'Ora et Labora' (Pray and Work), shaping Western civilization.

name: St. Bernadette Soubirous
profession: Sisters of Charity of Nevers & Lourdes Visionary
summary: Humble shepherd girl to whom the Immaculate Conception appeared eighteen times at the grotto of Massabielle in Lourdes.

name: St. Bernard of Clairvaux
profession: Cistercian Abbot, Reformer & Mellifluous Doctor (Doctor Mellifluus)
summary: Major Cistercian reformer, contemplative mystic, and adviser to popes and kings, renowned for fervent Marian devotion and theological eloquence.

name: St. Blaise
summary: Bishop and physician martyred in Armenia who famously saved a young boy choking on a fishbone; honored with the annual Blessing of the Throats.

name: St. Bonaventure
profession: Cardinal Bishop, Minister General of Franciscans & Seraphic Doctor (Doctor Seraphicus)
summary: Franciscan philosopher and theologian who synthesized mystical devotion and scholastic philosophy in works like The Mind's Road to God.

name: St. Bridget of Sweden (Birgitta)
summary: Swedish noblewoman and mother of eight who experienced mystical revelations of the Passion of Christ, founded the Bridgettine Order, and worked for papal return to Rome.

name: St. Brigid of Kildare
profession: Abbess & Co-Patroness of Ireland (Mary of the Gael)
patronage: Ireland, Dairy Workers, Nuns, Healers, Poets
summary: Founded the great monastic community of Kildare, renowned for generous hospitality, miracles of healing, and weaving the Brigid's Cross.

name: St. Bruno of Cologne
summary: Distinguished theology master who withdrew to the isolated valley of the Grande Chartreuse to found the contemplative Carthusians, dedicated to unbroken prayer and silence.

name: St. Camillus de Lellis
profession: Priest & Founder of the Camillians (Ministers of the Sick)
patronage: Hospitals, Nurses, Sick People, Healthcare Workers
summary: Former gambler and soldier who founded the Order of Clerks Regular, Ministers to the Sick (Camillians), pioneering modern emergency medicine and hospital care.

name: St. Carlo Acutis
profession: Student, Programmer & Cyber-Apostle of the Eucharist
patronage: Youth, Students, Programmers, Computer Users, Internet, Webmasters, Digital Evangelization
summary: Italian teenager and computer programmer (often celebrated as St. Carlos Acutis) who documented Eucharistic miracles and approved Marian apparitions on a website he designed before dying of leukemia at age 15, offering his suffering for the Church and the Pope.

name: St. Casimir
profession: Crown Prince of Poland & Grand Duchy of Lithuania
summary: Royal prince known for heroic chastity, love of the poor, intense Marian devotion (celebrated through the hymn Omni die dic Mariae), and peaceful statecraft.

name: St. Catherine of Bologna
summary: Italian Poor Clare abbess, calligrapher, and mystic whose spiritual reflections and preserved paintings inspired Renaissance religious devotion.

name: St. Catherine of Siena
profession: Dominican Tertiary, Mystic & Co-Patron of Europe
summary: Dominican mystic who counseled Pope Gregory XI to return the papacy from Avignon to Rome. Author of The Dialogue and patron of Europe.

name: St. Cecilia
summary: Roman noble martyr who sang in her heart to God during her wedding and survived executioners before surrendering her spirit.

name: St. Charbel Makhlouf
patronage: Lebanon, Unity of Christians, Miraculous Healings
summary: Maronite monk and hermit who lived twenty-three years of solitary prayer, fasting, and Eucharistic contemplation, source of thousands of documented healings.

name: St. Charles Borromeo
profession: Cardinal Archbishop of Milan & Council of Trent Reformer
summary: Leading figure of the Council of Trent, instituted modern seminary education and personally nursed plague victims in Milan.

name: St. Charles de Foucauld
summary: French explorer and soldier who experienced deep conversion, living as a hermit among the Tuareg in the Algerian Sahara as a 'universal brother'.

name: St. Charles Lwanga & the Ugandan Martyrs
profession: Royal Page & 22 Catholic Martyrs of Uganda
patronage: African Youth, Catholic Action, Torture Victims
summary: Chief page in the court of Mwanga II who protected younger pages and willingly chose martyrdom by fire at Namugongo for refusing to renounce Christ.

name: St. Christopher
summary: Early Christian martyr commemorated for carrying a child across a dangerous river, discovering the child was Christ carrying the weight of the whole world.

name: St. Clare of Assisi
profession: Foundress of the Poor Clares & Contemplative
summary: First follower of St. Francis who founded the Order of Poor Ladies (Poor Clares) and protected her monastery by raising the Blessed Sacrament against invaders.

name: St. Clare of Montefalco (St. Clare of the Cross)
summary: Augustinian contemplative mystic who devoted her life to the Passion of Christ; upon her death, symbols of the Crucifixion were found imprinted upon her heart.

name: St. Clement of Rome
summary: Fourth Pope of the Catholic Church who wrote the historic Epistle to the Corinthians asserting apostolic succession and unity within the Church.

name: St. Columba of Iona (Colmcille)
summary: One of the Twelve Apostles of Ireland who founded the influential abbey of Iona off the Scottish coast, leading the Christianization of the Picts and Scots.

name: St. Columbanus
summary: Irish missionary abbot who established monastic communities across the Frankish and Lombard kingdoms, including Luxeuil and Bobbio, reviving Christian culture across Europe.

name: St. Cuthbert of Lindisfarne
summary: Beloved Anglo-Saxon prior and bishop known for his pastoral journeys across the border hills, deep prayer life on Inner Farne, and posthumous incorrupt relics.

name: St. Cyril of Alexandria
summary: Leader at the Council of Ephesus (431) defending Mary as Theotokos (Mother of God) against Nestorianism and affirming the hypostatic union of Christ.

name: St. Cyril of Jerusalem
summary: Delivered the celebrated Catechetical Lectures illuminating baptism, confirmation, the Eucharist, and the Creed for early Christian converts.

name: St. Damasus I
profession: Pope & Patron of the Latin Vulgate
summary: 37th Pope who preserved the catacombs with carved epigrams and commissioned St. Jerome to produce the Latin Vulgate translation of the Sacred Scriptures.

name: St. Damien of Molokai
profession: Priest (Picpus Fathers) & Apostle to the Lepers
patronage: Leprosy, Hawaii, Outcasts, People with HIV/AIDS
summary: Volunteered to minister indefinitely to the banished leper colony on the island of Molokai, building homes and churches until succumbing to the disease.

name: St. Dominic de Guzmán
profession: Priest & Founder of the Order of Preachers (Dominicans)
summary: Founded the Order of Preachers (Dominicans) committed to rigorous study, itinerant poverty, combating heresy, and praying the Holy Rosary.

name: St. Dominic Savio
summary: Pupil of Don Bosco who lived by the motto 'Death rather than sin' and showed that holiness is reachable even in youth before dying at fourteen.

name: St. Dunstan
summary: English monastic reformer, skilled artisan, and statesman who restored monastic life in England and devised the royal coronation service still used today.

name: St. Edmund Campion
profession: Jesuit Priest & Martyr (Forty Martyrs of England and Wales)
summary: Brilliant Oxford scholar who entered the Society of Jesus and returned secretly to England to minister to underground Catholics, composing 'Campion's Brag' before his martyrdom at Tyburn.

name: St. Edward the Confessor
profession: King of England & Founder of Westminster Abbey
patronage: Kings, Difficult Marriages, Separated Spouses, England
summary: Pious Anglo-Saxon monarch renowned for his charity, justice, preserved chastity in marriage, and construction of Westminster Abbey.

name: St. Elizabeth Ann Seton
profession: Foundress (Sisters of Charity) & Catholic School Pioneer
patronage: Catholic Schools, Educators, Loss of Parents, Widows
summary: First native-born American canonized saint. Established the first free Catholic girls' school in America and founded the Sisters of Charity of St. Joseph.

name: St. Elizabeth of Hungary
profession: Princess of Hungary & Third Order Franciscan
patronage: Bakers, Beggars, Charitable Societies, Hospitals, Widows
summary: Hungarian princess who used her royal wealth to care for the sick and poor, joining the Third Order of St. Francis and establishing a hospital at Marburg.

name: St. Ephrem the Syrian
profession: Deacon, Hymnographer, Poet & Harp of the Holy Spirit
summary: Prolific Syriac poet, deacon, and theologian whose theological hymns combat heresies and glorify the mystery of the Incarnation and Blessed Mother.

name: St. Eric IX of Sweden (Eric the Holy)
summary: Swedish monarch who codified Christian laws, supported missionary work in Finland, and was martyred by Danish rebels after attending Ascension Day Mass.

name: St. Faustina Kowalska
profession: Sister of Our Lady of Mercy & Secretary of Divine Mercy
summary: Mystic entrusted with Jesus's message of Divine Mercy, resulting in the Divine Mercy Chaplet, the Image of Divine Mercy, and Divine Mercy Sunday.

name: St. Frances Xavier Cabrini (Mother Cabrini)
profession: Foundress (Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart)
summary: First United States citizen canonized. Built hospitals, schools, and orphanages across the Americas serving disenfranchised immigrant communities.

name: St. Francis Borgia
profession: Duke of Gandía & Third Superior General of the Jesuits
summary: Spanish grandee and Duke of Gandía who entered the Society of Jesus after the death of his wife and Empress Isabella, expanding Jesuit overseas missions across America and Asia.

name: St. Francis de Sales
profession: Bishop of Geneva, Writer & Doctor of Charity (Doctor Caritatis)
patronage: Writers, Catholic Journalists, the Deaf, Educators
summary: Gentle pastor and bishop who emphasized universal call to holiness in Introduction to the Devout Life and co-founded the Order of the Visitation.

name: St. Francis of Assisi
profession: Friar Minor & Founder of Franciscan Orders
summary: Renounced wealth to embrace Lady Poverty, rebuilt the Church by living the Gospel, received the stigmata on Mount La Verna.

name: St. Francis Xavier
profession: Jesuit Priest & Apostle of the Indies and Japan
summary: Co-founder of the Jesuits and one of history's greatest missionaries, baptizing hundreds of thousands across India, the Moluccas, and Japan.

name: St. Gabriel the Archangel
patronage: Messengers, Postal Workers, Telecommunications, Broadcasters, Diplomats, Radio Workers, Journalists
summary: The archangel of the Annunciation ('Strength of God') who interpreted visions for the prophet Daniel, announced the birth of John the Baptist to Zechariah, and delivered the heavenly greeting to the Virgin Mary that she would conceive the Son of God.

name: St. George
summary: Roman officer of the Guard who was tortured and beheaded for refusing to sacrifice to pagan gods; emblem of Christian chivalry.

name: St. Gertrude the Great (Gertrude of Helfta)
summary: German mystic of the monastery of Helfta, early visionary champion of the Sacred Heart of Jesus, and author of The Herald of Divine Love.

name: St. Gianna Beretta Molla
summary: Devout pediatrician and mother who chose to carry her fourth child to term knowing it risked her life, exemplifying sacrificial maternal love.

name: St. Giuseppe Moscati
summary: Pioneering medical researcher and physician in Naples who treated the poor for free and combined brilliant medical skill with holy personal piety.

name: St. Gregory of Narek
summary: Armenian monk whose masterpiece, The Book of Lamentations (Narek), is an enduring summit of mystical prayer, contrition, and lyrical theology.

name: St. Gregory of Nazianzus
summary: Cappadocian Father whose Five Theological Orations decisively shaped orthodox Trinitarian theology at the First Council of Constantinople (381).

name: St. Gregory the Great
profession: Pope, Monk, Reformer & Latin Church Father
summary: Benedictine pope known for pastoral care, liturgical and Gregorian chant reforms, and sending St. Augustine of Canterbury to evangelize England.

name: St. Hilary of Poitiers
profession: Bishop of Poitiers & The Hammer of the Arians (Malleus Arianorum)
summary: Staunch defender of the Council of Nicaea in the Western Church, author of De Trinitate, and influential early Latin Christian writer.

name: St. Hildegard of Bingen
profession: Benedictine Abbess, Polymath, Composer & Mystic (Sibyl of the Rhine)
summary: Benedictine abbess and universal genius who produced visionary theological works (Scivias), medicinal treatises, and liturgical music of transcendent beauty.

name: St. Ignatius of Antioch
profession: Bishop of Antioch, Apostolic Father & Martyr (Theophorus)
patronage: Church in the Eastern Mediterranean, Throat Diseases
summary: Third Bishop of Antioch and disciple of John who wrote seven profound pastoral epistles on the episcopacy and the Eucharist on his journey to Rome to be thrown to wild beasts.

name: St. Ignatius of Loyola
profession: Knight, Priest & Founder of the Society of Jesus (Jesuits)
summary: Wounded soldier converted during convalescence who authored the Spiritual Exercises and founded the Jesuits for the greater glory of God (AMDG).

name: St. Irenaeus of Lyons
profession: Bishop of Lugdunum, Martyr & Doctor of Unity (Doctor Unitatis)
summary: Disciple of St. Polycarp of Smyrna. Refuted Gnosticism in Against Heresies, defending apostolic tradition, the fourfold Gospel, and unity of faith.

name: St. Isidore of Seville
profession: Archbishop of Seville, Encyclopedist & Scholar (Doctor Egregius)
patronage: The Internet, Computer Users, Programmers, Students
summary: Last of the ancient Western Church Fathers. Compiled the Etymologiae, preserving Greco-Roman classical learning for medieval Europe.

name: St. Jacques Berthieu
profession: Jesuit Priest, Missionary & First Martyr of Madagascar
summary: French Jesuit priest who tirelessly evangelized rural Madagascar, murdered during the Menalamba rebellion for refusing to renounce his Christian faith.

name: St. James the Greater
patronage: Pilgrims, Spain, Santiago de Compostela, Laborers
summary: Son of Zebedee and brother of John, witnessed the Transfiguration and Agony in the Garden; first apostle martyred.

name: St. James the Lesser
profession: Apostle & Bishop of Jerusalem (James son of Alphaeus)
summary: Apostle and leader of the early Jerusalem Christian community who played a prominent role at the Council of Jerusalem and authored the Epistle of James.

name: St. Jane Frances de Chantal
profession: Foundress of the Order of the Visitation of Holy Mary
patronage: Widows, Forgotten People, Parents Separated from Children
summary: French noblewoman, mother, and widow who collaborated with St. Francis de Sales to found the Visitation Order for women rejected by other austere orders.

name: St. Jerome
summary: Translated Sacred Scripture from Hebrew and Greek into Latin (the Vulgate). Famously wrote: 'Ignorance of Scripture is ignorance of Christ.'

name: St. Joan of Arc
profession: Peasant Girl, Military Commander & Martyr (Maid of Orléans)
summary: Led French armies to victory during the Hundred Years' War guided by heavenly voices of St. Michael and St. Catherine, martyred at nineteen in Rouen.

name: St. John Berchmans
summary: Belgian Jesuit youth celebrated for achieving heroic sanctity through the perfection of ordinary daily duties and intense devotion to the Blessed Sacrament.

name: St. John Bosco (Don Bosco)
profession: Priest, Educator & Founder of the Salesians
summary: Pioneered the 'Preventive System' of education rooted in reason, religion, and loving-kindness, sheltering and mentoring disadvantaged youth in Turin.

name: St. John Chrysostom
summary: Renowned for fiery, eloquent preaching on social justice, repentance, and the Eucharist (the Divine Liturgy of St. John Chrysostom).

name: St. John Damascene
profession: Priest, Monk, Hymnographer & Defender of Icons
summary: Monk of Mar Saba near Jerusalem who defended holy images during the Iconoclast controversy and authored The Fountain of Wisdom.

name: St. John Henry Newman
patronage: Scholars, University Students, Converts, Catholic Education
summary: Leader of the Oxford Movement who entered full communion with the Catholic Church, author of The Idea of a University and Essay on the Development of Christian Doctrine.

name: St. John of Ávila
summary: Priest and master spiritual director who reformed Spanish clergy, mentored Teresa of Ávila and John of God, and wrote Audi, Filia.

name: St. John of Nepomuk
profession: Canon of Prague & Martyr of the Confessional
patronage: Confessors, Seal of Confession, Bridges, Floods, Bohemia
summary: Vicar General of Prague drowned in the Vltava River by King Wenceslaus IV for refusing to break the sacred seal of confession regarding the Queen's sins.

name: St. John of the Cross
profession: Carmelite Priest, Reformer, Poet & Mystical Doctor (Doctor Mysticus)
summary: Discalced Carmelite reformer alongside St. Teresa of Ávila. Author of sublime mystical treatises including Dark Night of the Soul and Ascent of Mount Carmel.

name: St. John Paul II (Karol Wojtyła)
profession: Pope, Philosopher, Poet & World Youth Day Founder
patronage: World Youth Day, Young Families, Krakow
summary: Pilgrim Pope who traveled to 129 countries, survived assassination, contributed to the fall of European communism, and authored Theology of the Body.

name: St. John the Apostle
summary: The disciple whom Jesus loved, stood at the foot of the Cross, entrusted with Mary, and author of the Fourth Gospel, three epistles, and Revelation.

name: St. John the Baptist
summary: The voice crying out in the wilderness preparing the way of the Lord. Baptized Jesus in the Jordan River and bore witness with his martyrdom.

name: St. John Vianney (Curé of Ars)
profession: Parish Priest of Ars & Patron of Parish Priests
summary: Humble French parish priest renowned for spending up to sixteen hours daily hearing confessions, spiritual discernment, and converting the village of Ars.

name: St. John XXIII (Angelo Roncalli)
profession: Pope (The Good Pope) & Initiator of Second Vatican Council
patronage: Papal Delegates, Second Vatican Council, Christian Unity
summary: Beloved 261st Pope who convened the Second Vatican Council (1962–1965) to promote pastoral renewal and Christian unity, author of Pacem in Terris.

name: St. José Sánchez del Río
summary: Fourteen-year-old Mexican Cristero youth who was tortured and killed during the Cristero War, crying out '¡Viva Cristo Rey!' with his dying breath.

name: St. Josemaría Escrivá
patronage: Opus Dei, Ordinary Work, Diabetes Sufferers
summary: Spanish priest who founded Opus Dei, teaching the universal call to holiness and sanctification of ordinary daily work and family life.

name: St. Joseph
patronage: Universal Church, Fathers, Workers, Carpenters, Dying, Unborn
summary: Husband of the Blessed Virgin Mary and foster father of Jesus Christ. Declared Patron of the Universal Church and Terror of Demons.

name: St. Joseph of Cupertino
patronage: Test Takers, Students, Aviators, Pilots, Air Travelers
summary: Humble Franciscan friar known for profound ecstatic levitations during prayer and Mass, venerated as the patron of struggling students and examinees.

name: St. Juan Diego Cuauhtlatoatzin
profession: Lay Hermit & Visionary of Our Lady of Guadalupe
summary: Humble Chichimeca layman to whom the Blessed Virgin Mary appeared at Tepeyac Hill as Our Lady of Guadalupe, leaving her miraculous image on his tilma.

name: St. Jude Thaddeus
profession: Apostle & Author of Epistle of Jude
summary: Apostle and author of the Epistle of Jude. Revered worldwide as the patron saint of impossible and desperate situations.

name: St. Junípero Serra
summary: Mallorcan Franciscan friar who founded nine of the twenty-one Spanish missions in California under the motto 'Siempre adelante' (Always forward).

name: St. Justin Martyr
summary: Early Christian philosopher who wrote the First and Second Apologies to the Roman Emperor defending Christian belief and providing the earliest detailed account of the Holy Mass.

name: St. Kateri Tekakwitha
summary: First Native American recognized as a saint. Converted to Catholicism despite harsh ostracism, living a life of heroic chastity, penance, and love for Christ.

name: St. Katharine Drexel
profession: Foundress of the Sisters of the Blessed Sacrament
patronage: Philanthropy, Racial Justice, Native and African Americans
summary: Philadelphia heiress who gave her entire inherited fortune to establish schools and missions for Native Americans and African Americans across the United States.

name: St. Andrew Kim Taegon & the Korean Martyrs
profession: First Native Korean Catholic Priest & 103 Martyrs
summary: First native Korean priest and 102 lay martyrs who planted and defended the Catholic faith in Joseon Korea during severe 19th-century persecutions.

name: Blessed Laura Vicuña
patronage: Abuse Victims, Argentina, Incest Victims, Loss of Parents
summary: Twelve-year-old Chilean Salesian student in Argentina who offered her life to God for the conversion and spiritual liberation of her mother.

name: St. Lawrence of Brindisi
profession: Capuchin Priest, Diplomat & Apostolic Doctor (Doctor Apostolicus)
summary: Linguist, diplomat, and Capuchin leader who preached throughout Europe, rallying forces against Ottoman expansion and converting many to the Catholic faith.

name: St. Lawrence of Rome
patronage: Deacons, Cooks, Chefs, Comedians, the Poor
summary: Deacon entrusted with Church treasures who presented the poor and sick as the true wealth of the Church before dying cheerfully upon a gridiron.

name: St. Leo the Great
profession: Pope & Latin Church Father (Doctor Unitatis Ecclesiae)
summary: Asserted papal primacy, confronted Attila the Hun to save Rome, and authored the Tome of Leo defining Christ's two natures at the Council of Chalcedon (451).

name: St. Lorenzo Ruiz
patronage: The Philippines, Filipino Migrant Workers, Poor
summary: First Filipino saint, martyred in Nagasaki, Japan. Proclaimed: 'I am a Catholic and will remain a Catholic until death. Even if I had a thousand lives, I would give them all to God.'

name: St. Louis IX of France
profession: King of France & Third Order Franciscan
patronage: France, Kings, Builders, Hairdressers, Secular Franciscans
summary: Devout French monarch celebrated for fair judicial reforms, feeding the poor from his own table, building Sainte-Chapelle, and leading crusades with deep Christian chivalry.

name: St. Louise de Marillac
profession: Foundress of the Daughters of Charity
summary: Collaborated with St. Vincent de Paul to organize rural relief and found the Daughters of Charity, pioneering non-cloistered religious life dedicated to serving the poor.

name: St. Lucy of Syracuse
summary: Martyr of Syracuse who distributed her dowry to the poor and stood unmovable through torment for the name of Christ.

name: St. Luke the Evangelist
summary: Beloved physician, traveling companion of St. Paul, and inspired author of the Third Gospel and the Acts of the Apostles.

name: St. Margaret Clitherow (Pearl of York)
summary: York housewife who hid Catholic priests and hosted secret Masses in her home, martyred by being pressed to death under heavy stones to protect her children from testifying.

name: St. Margaret of Scotland
summary: English princess who married King Malcolm III of Scotland, transforming court life through piety, education, charity, and church reforms.

name: St. Maria Goretti
summary: Eleven-year-old martyr who chose physical death rather than surrender her purity, forgiving her attacker from her deathbed.

name: St. Marianne Cope (Mother Marianne of Molokai)
summary: Sisters of Saint Francis of Syracuse leader who volunteered to care for quarantined Hansen's disease (leprosy) patients on Molokai, continuing St. Damien's mission.

name: St. Mark the Evangelist
profession: Companion of Peter and Paul & Evangelist
summary: Companion of St. Peter in Rome and founder of the Church of Alexandria; author of the Second Gospel.

name: St. Martin de Porres
patronage: Racial Harmony, Social Justice, Barbers, Public Health, Innkeepers
summary: Afro-Peruvian Dominican brother renowned for humility, spiritual gifts, caring for the sick of all races, and miraculous compassion for all living creatures.

name: St. Martin of Tours
profession: Roman Soldier, Bishop of Tours & Monastic Pioneer
patronage: Soldiers, Cavalry, Beggars, France, Wine Makers
summary: Roman soldier who famously cut his military cloak in half to clothe a freezing beggar, who was revealed in a vision as Jesus Christ; later founded French monasteries and became Bishop of Tours.

name: St. Mary MacKillop (St. Mary of the Cross)
profession: Foundress of the Sisters of St. Joseph of the Sacred Heart
summary: First canonized saint of Australia who co-founded the Josephites to establish free schools for impoverished rural children and shelters for orphans.

name: St. Mary Magdalene
profession: Disciple & Apostle to the Apostles (Apostola Apostolorum)
summary: Faithful follower of Christ who was the first witness to His Resurrection and heralded the Good News to the Apostles on Easter morning.

name: St. Matthew the Apostle
patronage: Accountants, Bankers, Tax Collectors, Customs Officers
summary: Left his tax booth upon Jesus's call: 'Follow me.' Authored the First Gospel directed to Jewish Christians.

name: St. Matthias
profession: Apostle chosen to replace Judas Iscariot
summary: Disciple chosen by lot among the followers of Jesus after the Ascension to complete the Twelve Apostles, witnessing Christ's resurrection.

name: St. Maximilian Kolbe
profession: Conventual Franciscan Friar, Publisher & Martyr of Charity
summary: Franciscan missionary who founded the Militia Immaculatae and gave his life voluntarily in the starvation bunker at Auschwitz in place of a stranger.

name: St. Mechtilde of Hackeborn
summary: Choirmistress and mystic at the Helfta monastery whose heavenly visions and deep liturgical spirituality were recorded in The Book of Special Grace.

name: St. Michael the Archangel
profession: Archangel, Prince of the Heavenly Host & Defender of the Church
patronage: Police Officers, Military, Soldiers, Paramedics, Grocers, Mariners, Radiologists, The Dying, Protection Against Evil
summary: Leader of the heavenly host ('Who is like God?') who cast Lucifer and the rebel angels out of heaven in the Book of Revelation. Revered as the defender of the Church, guardian of the faithful, and champion in spiritual warfare.

name: Blessed Miguel Pro
summary: Mexican Jesuit priest who carried out clandestine pastoral ministry disguised in various occupations during the Calles presidency before execution by firing squad.

name: St. Teresa of Calcutta (Mother Teresa)
profession: Foundress of the Missionaries of Charity
patronage: Missionaries of Charity, World Youth Day, the Poor
summary: Nobel laureate who served 'the poorest of the poor' in the slums of Calcutta, answering Jesus's call to quench His thirst on the Cross.

name: St. Nicholas of Myra
patronage: Children, Sailors, Merchants, Pawnbrokers, Russia, Greece
summary: Generous Bishop of Myra famed for secret gift-giving, defending the poor, and attending the Council of Nicaea; the historical inspiration for Santa Claus.

name: St. Nimatullah Kassab Al-Hardini
summary: Lebanese Maronite monk and teacher of St. Charbel Makhlouf, renowned for deep adoration of the Blessed Sacrament, humble manual labor, and binding books.

name: St. Olaf II of Norway
profession: King of Norway & Martyr (Rex Perpetuus Norvegiae)
summary: King of Norway who unified his country and introduced Christian laws; slain in the Battle of Stiklestad and venerated as the Eternal King of Norway.

name: St. Óscar Romero
patronage: El Salvador, Americas, Persecuted Christians, Human Rights
summary: Archbishop of San Salvador who courageously spoke out against social injustice, poverty, and state violence, assassinated while celebrating Holy Mass.

name: St. Pachomius the Great
summary: Desert Father who founded the first Christian communal monasteries along the Nile, establishing written monastic rules that shaped Eastern and Western monastic life.

name: St. Pio of Pietrelcina (Padre Pio)
summary: Capuchin priest who bore the stigmata for fifty years, gifted with bilocation and reading souls in the confessional; famous for: 'Pray, hope, and don't worry.'

name: St. Pancras of Rome
patronage: Children, Jobs, Employment, False Witness Protection
summary: Fourteen-year-old orphan convert who was beheaded under Emperor Diocletian for refusing to offer sacrifice to pagan gods.

name: St. Patrick
summary: Kidnapped into Irish slavery as a youth, escaped, then returned as bishop to evangelize the Irish people and establish churches across the island.

name: St. Paul Miki & Companions (Twenty-Six Martyrs of Japan)
summary: Japanese Jesuit preacher who, along with twenty-five Franciscan and Jesuit companions, was crucified on a hill in Nagasaki, forgiving his executioners from the cross.

name: St. Paul of the Cross
profession: Priest, Mystic & Founder of the Passionists
summary: Italian preacher and mystic who founded the Congregation of the Passion (Passionists) to promote memory of Christ's Passion as the most efficacious remedy for moral evils.

name: St. Paul the Apostle
profession: Tentmaker, Apostle to the Gentiles & Author of Epistles
summary: Converted on the road to Damascus after persecuting the Church. Prolific missionary whose epistles comprise much of the New Testament.

name: St. Paul the First Hermit
summary: Regarded by St. Jerome as the first Christian hermit, who lived over ninety years of prayer and contemplation alone in the Egyptian desert fed daily by a raven.

name: St. Paul VI (Giovanni Battista Montini)
profession: Pope & Concluder of Second Vatican Council
summary: 262nd Pope who brought the Second Vatican Council to completion, promulgated the Missal of Paul VI, and authored the encyclical Humanae Vitae.

name: St. Pedro Calungsod
summary: Teenage Visayan catechist missionary in Guam who assisted Fr. Diego Luis de San Vitores and was martyred while defending his priest with heroic courage.

name: Sts. Perpetua and Felicity
patronage: Mothers, Pregnant Women, Expectant Mothers, Butchers
summary: Noblewoman Perpetua and her enslaved companion Felicity, young mothers who fearlessly stood firm in their faith and were martyred in the amphitheater at Carthage.

name: St. Peter Canisius
profession: Jesuit Priest, Catechist & Second Apostle of Germany
summary: Key leader of the Catholic Counter-Reformation in Central Europe, establishing Jesuit colleges and authoring widely used catechisms.

name: St. Peter Chrysologus
profession: Archbishop of Ravenna & Doctor of Short Sermons (Golden-Worded)
summary: Archbishop of Ravenna renowned for concise, luminous homilies explaining the Incarnation, the Apostles' Creed, and Christian moral life.

name: St. Peter Claver
profession: Jesuit Priest & 'Slave of the Slaves Forever'
patronage: African Missions, Human Rights, Colombia, Interracial Justice
summary: Spanish Jesuit missionary who spent forty years at the port of Cartagena ministering to enslaved Africans, personally feeding, tending, and baptizing over 300,000 people.

name: St. Peter Damian
profession: Benedictine Monk, Cardinal Bishop & Church Reformer
summary: Camaldolese monk and cardinal who spearheaded Gregorian reforms, combating simony and clerical corruption with rigorous ascetical discipline.

name: St. Peter the Apostle
summary: Leader of the Twelve Apostles, given the keys of the kingdom of heaven by Jesus Christ. Martyred in Rome by crucifixion upside-down.

name: St. Philip Howard
patronage: Difficult Marriages, Atticus Patients, Betrayed Spouses
summary: English nobleman and courtier who converted to Catholicism, spending ten years imprisoned in the Tower of London for his faith until his death.

name: St. Philip Neri
summary: Joyful Roman priest whose warm humor, street ministry, and musical gatherings at the Oratory revitalized the spiritual heart of Rome.

name: St. Philip the Apostle
summary: Apostle from Bethsaida who brought Nathanael (Bartholomew) to Jesus and asked the Lord to 'show us the Father' at the Last Supper.

name: St. Pius X (Giuseppe Sarto)
profession: Pope & Reformer of Church Music and Canon Law
summary: 257th Pope who lowered the age of First Communion to the age of discretion, encouraged frequent reception of the Eucharist, and initiated the 1917 Code of Canon Law.

name: St. Polycarp of Smyrna
summary: Disciple of St. John the Apostle and Bishop of Smyrna. Martyred by fire and sword after famously declaring he could not blaspheme the King who had saved him for 86 years.

name: St. Rafqa Pietra Choboq Ar-Rayès (Rebecca)
patronage: Loss of Parents, Sick People, Blindness, Bodily Ills
summary: Maronite nun who joyfully united her intense physical suffering—blindness and paralysis—with the Passion of Jesus Christ in total serenity and love.

name: St. Raphael the Archangel
patronage: Travelers, The Blind, Physicians, Nurses, Pharmacists, Medical Workers, Matchmakers, Lovers, Healers
summary: The archangel of healing ('God heals') who disguised himself as Azarias to guide Tobias on his journey in the Book of Tobit, healed Tobit's blindness with fish gall, delivered Sarah from demonic oppression, and revealed himself as one of the seven angels who stand in the glorious presence of the Lord.

name: St. Rita of Cascia
patronage: Impossible Causes, Difficult Marriages, Infertility, Wounded Sufferers
summary: Italian mystic and Augustinian sister who bore the sorrow of a difficult marriage, family tragedy, and received a miraculous partial stigmata wound of the Crown of Thorns.

name: St. Robert Bellarmine
summary: Leading apologist of the Counter-Reformation, author of Disputationes de Controversiis, and spiritual director to St. Aloysius Gonzaga.

name: St. Roch (St. Rocco)
patronage: Plague Sufferers, Epidemics, Dogs, Invalids, Knee Problems
summary: French nobleman who distributed his wealth to pilgrims and cured plague victims across Italy, comforted during his own sickness by a faithful dog that brought him bread.

name: St. Romuald
profession: Abbot & Founder of the Camaldolese Order
summary: Italian ascetic and reformer who combined Eastern eremitic solitude with Western cenobitic community life in founding the Camaldolese monastic family.

name: St. Rose of Lima (Isabel Flores de Oliva)
profession: Third Order Dominican & First Canonized Saint of the Americas
patronage: The Americas, Peru, Florists, Gardeners, Embroiderers
summary: Peruvian mystic and tertiary Dominican renowned for her beauty, intense prayer, penance, and loving service to the sick and impoverished.

name: St. Scholastica
summary: Twin sister of St. Benedict who led Benedictine nuns, celebrated for her deep prayer life that moved God to send a storm so she could converse with her brother.

name: St. Sebastian
summary: Imperial guard officer who secretly aided imprisoned Christians, survived being shot with arrows, and was beaten to death for confronting the Emperor.

name: St. Simon the Zealot
summary: One of the Twelve Apostles, known for his zeal for the Jewish law before following Christ, who preached the Gospel in Egypt and Persia.

name: St. Stanislaus Kostka
summary: Young Polish noble who walked hundreds of miles to Rome to fulfill his vocation in the Society of Jesus, dying in holiness at age seventeen.

name: St. Stephen
summary: First Christian martyr, full of grace and power, who prayed for his persecutors as he was stoned to death outside Jerusalem.

name: St. Stephen I of Hungary
profession: First King of Hungary & Apostolic King
summary: First King of Hungary who united the Magyar tribes, established the Church throughout the kingdom, and dedicated his nation to the Blessed Virgin Mary.

name: St. Tarcisius
summary: Young Roman acolyte beaten to death by a pagan mob while carrying the Blessed Sacrament to imprisoned Christians, choosing death rather than surrender the Holy Eucharist.

name: St. Teresa Benedicta of the Cross (Edith Stein)
profession: Discalced Carmelite Nun, Philosopher & Patroness of Europe
patronage: Europe, Loss of Parents, Philosophers, Converts, Martyrs
summary: Jewish-born phenomenologist philosopher who converted to Catholicism, entered the Carmelites, and was martyred at Auschwitz-Birkenau in solidarity with her people.

name: St. Teresa of Ávila
profession: Carmelite Nun, Reformer & Seraphic Mother (Doctor of Prayer)
patronage: Spain, Illness, Loss of Parents, People in Need of Grace
summary: First female Doctor of the Church. Reformed the Carmelites and wrote spiritual masterpieces on contemplation such as The Interior Castle and The Way of Perfection.

name: St. Thérèse of Lisieux
profession: Discalced Carmelite Nun (The Little Flower, Doctor Amoris)
summary: Carmelite nun known for her 'Little Way' of spiritual childhood, trust, and complete abandonment to God's merciful love in Story of a Soul.

name: St. Thomas Aquinas
profession: Dominican Friar, Philosopher, Theologian & Angelic Doctor (Doctor Angelicus)
patronage: Academics, Students, Theologians, Catholic Schools, Apologists
summary: Master of scholastic theology whose Summa Theologiae and Eucharistic hymns (such as Pange Lingua and Panis Angelicus) form the foundation of Catholic doctrine and philosophy.

name: St. Thomas Becket
summary: Lord Chancellor who was made Archbishop of Canterbury and steadfastly defended the rights and independence of the Church against King Henry II, martyred in his cathedral.

name: St. Thomas More
profession: Lord Chancellor of England, Statesman & Martyr
summary: Statesman and author of Utopia who chose death rather than compromise his conscience against King Henry VIII: 'The King's good servant, but God's first.'

name: St. Thomas the Apostle
summary: Famous for his confession 'My Lord and my God!' after seeing the risen Christ. Evangelized Persia and India, where he was martyred.

name: St. Timothy
profession: Bishop of Ephesus & Disciple of St. Paul
summary: Beloved disciple and companion of St. Paul who became the first Bishop of Ephesus and received two Pauline pastoral epistles.

name: St. Titus
profession: Bishop of Crete & Disciple of St. Paul
summary: Gentile convert and trusted co-worker of St. Paul who was appointed Bishop of Crete to organize the local church and ordain presbyters.

name: St. Titus Brandsma
profession: Carmelite Priest, Professor & Martyr of Dachau
patronage: Catholic Journalists, The Netherlands, Press Freedom
summary: Dutch Carmelite friar and university rector who defied Nazi anti-Catholic propaganda and press censorship, murdered by lethal injection in Dachau concentration camp.

name: St. Turibius of Mogrovejo
patronage: Latin American Bishops, Native Rights, Peru
summary: Archbishop of Lima who traveled over 15,000 miles across the Andes on foot, learning indigenous languages and defending native peoples' human dignity.

name: St. Valentine of Rome
patronage: Love, Marriages, Betrothed Couples, Beekeepers, Epilepsy
summary: Roman clergyman who ministered to persecuted Christians and performed secret marriages for Christian soldiers, martyred during the reign of Claudius Gothicus.

name: The Vietnamese Martyrs (St. Andrew Dũng-Lạc & Companions)
patronage: Vietnam, Vietnamese People, Persecuted Christians, Catechists, Martyrs
summary: A collective group of 117 martyrs—including Vietnamese diocesan priest St. Andrew Dũng-Lạc, 96 Vietnamese Catholics, 11 Spanish Dominicans, and 10 French missionaries—who were executed between 1745 and 1862 under the persecution of the Trịnh and Nguyễn dynasties for their steadfast Christian faith.

name: St. Vincent de Paul
summary: Dedicated his priesthood to the relief of the impoverished and sick, founding the Vincentian Fathers and co-founding Daughters of Charity.

name: St. Wenceslaus (Václav)
profession: Duke of Bohemia & Martyr (Good King Wenceslas)
summary: Righteous Duke of Bohemia raised by St. Ludmila who promoted Christianity and justice, murdered by his pagan brother Boleslaus and immortalized as a model of Christian charity.
